research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-salvage/activation-curation.md:3:The new record represents exact **MetaCyc:PWY-7971**, the five-reaction activation subpathway that ends at adenosylcobinamide-GDP. It does not establish coverage of the larger COBALSYN-PWY or the separate late nucleotide-loop pathway PWY-5509. The inspected public MetaCyc/EcoCyc XML identifies version **22.5**; this is not a claim to the latest proprietary database release. Current reviewed UniProt inputs are release **2026_03**.
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-salvage/nucleotide-loop-curation.md:1:# PWY-5509 nucleotide-loop assembly
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-salvage/nucleotide-loop-curation.md:5:The initial ignored-inclusive search covered the accessible 169-record worktree and its research artifacts. Existing methionine and succinate-to-propanoate records use cobalamin as cofactor and do not duplicate nucleotide-loop biosynthesis. The older cobalamin handoff/native projection were read, including previously deferred exact pathway alternatives. The original Documents repository could not be searched because the OS denies access; no fresh original-checkout absence claim is made. The exact command, exclusions, output digests and limitation are in `nucleotide-loop-dedup.json`.
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-salvage/nucleotide-loop-curation.md:23:Several SI chemistry names are inconsistent: nicotinate ribonucleotide is abbreviated NMN; the CobS product and CobC substrate are written as adenosylcobinamide-5-P; Table2 footnote[4] calls phosphatase CobC a synthase. These are retained as source conflicts and are not imported into the graph. The Table1 right-hand values are **calculated K′eq**, not measured catalytic rates. Exact reactions follow independently inspected Rhea and reviewed UniProt. CobC[3] in the same supplement is a different organism's threonine-phosphate decarboxylase; only CobC[4] is the selected phosphatase.
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-salvage/nucleotide-loop-curation.md:31:`nucleotide-loop-source-manifest.json` records exact body hashes and canonical URLs, including27 rehashed bodies. It distinguishes the correct MOESM3 SI from an initially retrieved reporting-summary PDF and an HTML response masquerading as a PDF. The 2020 publisher full text was available through the web tool despite direct403 responses; no downloaded full-text digest is fabricated. `nucleotide-loop-source-projection.json` preserves the exact source fields, primary locators and conflicts; `nucleotide-loop-identifiers.json` enumerates all22 named nodes and21 reference identifiers with authority locators. Large ontology databases use existing source metadata plus direct SQL field inspection; they are not loaded wholesale into memory for hashing.
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-salvage/nucleotide-loop-curation.md:33:Run `nucleotide-loop-replay.py` in the documented external-cache layout to reconstruct the native/source projection and balance checks. Its writes are confined to the external nucleotide-loop scratch directory. All body hashes are streamed. The author target checks and their exact results are in `nucleotide-loop-validation.json`; they do not substitute for the independent scientific review or root's full integrated gates.
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-next/cobalamin-handoff.md:11:The independent native MetaCyc object **COBALSYN-PWY** is “superpathway of adenosylcobalamin salvage from cobinamide I,” containing **PWY-7971** (adenosylcobinamide-GDP salvage from cobinamide I) and **PWY-5509** (adenosylcobalamin biosynthesis from adenosylcobinamide-GDP I). The fetched public XML identifies MetaCyc version 22.5; it is not represented as the latest proprietary release. The native objects explicitly separate activation from nucleotide-loop assembly. E. coli salvage must not be labeled de novo corrin-ring synthesis. [Native superpathway](https://solcyc.sgn.cornell.edu/ECOLI/NEW-IMAGE?object=COBALSYN-PWY&type=PATHWAY).
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-next/cobalamin-handoff.md:29:**PMID10518530** directly reconstitutes nucleotide-loop assembly using **Salmonella typhimurium** enzymes. Results and methods identify the phosphorylated final intermediate and CobC dephosphorylation; E. coli BL21 used to express a construct is not evidence that the enzyme itself is E. coli. **PMID17209023**, inspected through its primary abstract, reassesses terminal CobC dephosphorylation specifically in **Salmonella enterica**. These support pathway chemistry and a homology rationale, not direct E. coli CobC characterization. [1999 primary paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC18366/), [2007 primary abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17209023/).
research/pathway_additions/2026-10-10-next/methylglyoxal-curation.md:20:- **Zinc and nucleotide conditions:** The 2019 GldA crystal contains zinc at the glycerol-bound active site; its NAD+ was modeled from another structure. UniProt zinc cofactor evidence is ECO:0000305 while the one-zinc-per-subunit note is ECO:0000269. These limits are preserved. The PMID6365902 complete abstract describes both NADH and NADPH supporting hydroxyacetone reduction; retaining the named pathway's NADH branch does not assert NADPH exclusion. No new NADPH second-step reaction or catalytic-site claim is invented from this abstract.
